description: The chain directory names the two arms of memphis_chain_verify used to disagree about. The native arm refused every archive directory (a dot is not in [A-Za-z0-9_-]), so 'verify all chains' aborted on the first archive and checked nothing. The TypeScript arm skipped them and kept going. {HOME} = <home>. The fixture holds the directory names only — the verifier's decision about a name is what both arms must agree on. MEASURED 2026-11-22: the first twelve cases were NOT enough — both runners were green while the rules still disagreed, because none of the cases reached a shape where they differ. The rules are the TypeScript registry's (SAFE_CHAIN_NAME: one to sixty-four characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-], plus the two archive stamp forms), and the native arm accepted three shapes the registry refuses: a plain name of sixty-five characters, and the dated archive stamp with a shape that is not YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-mmmZ. The corpus now reaches them.

cases.name: a plain chain name is scannable
a plain chain name with a digit suffix is scannable
an underscore in a chain name is scannable
a numeric archive suffix is an archive and therefore scannable
a dated archive suffix is an archive and therefore scannable
a second archive of another chain is an archive too
a parent traversal is not scannable
a nested path is not scannable
a backslash path is not scannable
a dot that is not an archive suffix is not scannable
an archive without a stamp is not an archive
an empty name is not scannable
a plain name of sixty-four characters is scannable
a plain name of sixty-five characters is not scannable
an archive of a long chain name is still an archive
an archive stamp that is not the dated form is not an archive
an archive stamp of the right length in the wrong shape is not an archive
